disease_label_per_paper: Klebsiella pneumoniae brain abscess in an immunocompetent patient
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 46-year-old Vietnamese American man with hypertension presented with progressive altered mental status, incoherent speech, personality change, and gait dysfunction.
Family reported mild left facial twitching, bizarre behavior, and locking himself in his bedroom for four days before admission.
Initial vital signs were temperature 37.1 C, heart rate 87/min, blood pressure 150/87 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Neurologic exam showed disorientation, obstinate affect, echolalic or mimicking speech, lethargy, GCS 14, right conjugate gaze, right lower facial weakness, and right dysmetria.
Brain MRI showed a 4.2 x 4.0 x 3.9 cm left frontal and temporal ring-enhancing mass with vasogenic edema, 1.1 cm midline shift, and mild hydrocephalus, concerning for brain abscess.

He underwent urgent drainage, but intraoperative pus spillage into the ventricles was followed by cerebritis, persistent abscess, septic shock, cerebral edema, refractory intracranial hypertension, multi-organ failure, and death on hospital day 14.
